SCRIPT
 import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import pandas as pd

regions = ['East Asia & Pacific', 'South Asia', 'Sub-Saharan Africa', 'Latin America & Caribbean']
years = list(range(1980, 1990))
coal_rents = {
    'East Asia & Pacific': [0.002, 0.003, 0.005, 0.008, 0.012, 0.015, 0.018, 0.022, 0.028, 0.035],
    'South Asia': [0.045, 0.052, 0.068, 0.085, 0.102, 0.115, 0.132, 0.148, 0.165, 0.188],
    'Sub-Saharan Africa': [0.015, 0.020, 0.028, 0.035, 0.040, 0.048, 0.055, 0.060, 0.068, 0.078],
    'Latin America & Caribbean': [0.005, 0.008, 0.012, 0.018, 0.025, 0.032, 0.038, 0.042, 0.048, 0.058]
}

oil_rents = {
    'East Asia & Pacific': [0.05, 0.06, 0.08, 0.10, 0.12, 0.15, 0.18, 0.22, 0.25, 0.28],
    'South Asia': [0.008, 0.009, 0.012, 0.015, 0.020, 0.025, 0.030, 0.038, 0.042, 0.048],
    'Sub-Saharan Africa': [0.12, 0.15, 0.18, 0.20, 0.22, 0.25, 0.28, 0.30, 0.32, 0.35],
    'Latin America & Caribbean': [0.15, 0.18, 0.22, 0.25, 0.30, 0.35, 0.40, 0.42, 0.45, 0.48]
}

data = []
for region in regions:
    for year, coal, oil in zip(years, coal_rents[region], oil_rents[region]):
        data.append([region, year, coal, oil])

df = pd.DataFrame(data, columns=['Region', 'Year', 'Coal_Rents', 'Oil_Rents'])
pivot_df = df.pivot(index='Region', columns='Year', values='Coal_Rents')

plt.figure(figsize=(12, 6))
sns.set_theme(style="white")
heatmap = sns.heatmap(
    pivot_df,
    annot=True,
    fmt=".3f",
    cmap="YlOrBr",
    cbar_kws={'label': 'Coal Rents (% of GDP)'},
    linewidths=0.5,
    linecolor='lightgray'
)

plt.title('Renewable Energy Consumption Growth by Region (1980-1989)', pad=20)
plt.xlabel('Region')
plt.ylabel('Year')
plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('output.png')

SUMMARY
 This image is a heatmap that illustrates coal rents as a percentage of GDP across four different regions from 1980 to 1989. The chart uses a gradient color scale ranging from light yellow to dark brown, where lighter shades represent lower percentages and darker shades signify higher percentages of GDP. The regions listed on the vertical axis are East Asia & Pacific, Latin America & Caribbean, South Asia, and Sub-Saharan Africa, while the horizontal axis spans the years 1980 to 1989.

Each cell within the heatmap contains a numerical value indicating the coal rents as a percentage of GDP for a specific region and year. For the East Asia & Pacific region, the values start at 0.002% in 1980 and gradually increase to 0.035% by 1989. Latin America & Caribbean displays slightly higher values, beginning at 0.005% in 1980 and rising to 0.058% in 1989. Sub-Saharan Africa shows a moderate increase from 0.015% in 1980 to 0.078% in 1989. South Asia consistently exhibits the highest coal rents among the regions, starting at 0.045% in 1980 and peaking at 0.188% in 1989.

The color intensity of the cells corresponds to the numerical values, with South Asia's cells appearing much darker due to its higher coal rent percentages, particularly in the later years of the decade. This visual representation effectively highlights the differences in coal rents as a proportion of GDP both across regions and over time.

p.write_text(s)
exec(compile(s, "chart.py", "exec"))
ax = plt.gca()
print("Title:", ax.get_title())
print("Axis labels:", ax.get_xlabel(), "/", ax.get_ylabel())
